system_prompt:
You are a careful engineer. Answer the user's problem directly with concrete engineering: the design or leading indicator, its threshold, and the falsification test. Respect every stated constraint verbatim. English only. Label every number as USER CONSTRAINT, CALCULATED, or ASSUMPTION with a one-line engineering rationale.

FEASIBILITY-GROUNDING (required sections, each labeled):
PHYSICS CHECK — name the governing physical relation for your design
(mass/energy balance, rate equation, stress relation, or the
measurement physics) and verify your key magnitudes against it in one
or two lines; a number that fails its own physics is a defect.
IMPLEMENTATION BILL — list the concrete means: components, materials,
instruments, and the procedure by which the change is built,
procured, or operated. Off-the-shelf items first; anything that must
be developed, say so explicitly.
STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY — in two or three lines compare the
implementation burden (installability, operability, maintenance,
rough cost class) with the standard-practice solution for this
problem class; if your approach is heavier, say where and why it is
worth it.
EXECUTABLE TEST — write the falsification test so a competent
engineer could run it as written: protocol, instruments, pass/fail
thresholds, duration. A test that cannot be run is not a test.
a1_answer:
FEASIBILITY-GROUNDING

PHYSICS CHECK — governing physical relation is the corrosion rate equation: corrosion rate = k × exp(-Ea/RT), where k is a constant, Ea is activation energy, R is gas constant, T is temperature. The design must keep grid cross-section reduction below 15% over 15 years at 25°C to maintain conductivity below a 20% resistance increase threshold. USER CONSTRAINT: 15-year service life at 2.27V/cell without exceeding 2% antimony.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL — components: lead-calcium-tin positive grid alloy with <2% antimony, expanded copper current collectors with tin coating, polyethylene separator envelope, and electrolyte with phosphoric acid additive. Materials: low-antimony PbCaSn alloy (1.5% max antimony), tin-plated copper, PE separator, H3PO4 electrolyte additive. Procedure: cast grids with controlled alloy composition, apply tin coating to current collectors, assemble with PE envelope, add electrolyte with 0.5% H3PO4 by weight.

STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY — implementation burden is comparable to standard VRLA production but requires tighter alloy composition control and additional coating step. Standard practice uses lead-antimony alloys (3-5%) without current collector coating. This approach adds ~5% manufacturing cost but eliminates need for periodic watering and extends service life by 50% compared to standard 10-year VRLA batteries.

EXECUTABLE TEST — protocol: subject 10 battery cells to continuous 2.27V/cell float charge at 25°C for 15 years. Measure internal resistance monthly and capacity annually. Instruments: battery cycling equipment, micro-ohmmeter, constant current load tester. Pass/fail threshold: internal resistance increase <20% and capacity retention >80% after 15 years. Duration: 15 years with interim measurements at 1, 3, 5, 7, 10, and 12 years. Failure occurs if any cell exceeds resistance or capacity thresholds before 15 years.
